sec: Wilson's screening algorithm, Nazar index and chelation pharmacotherapy

items.q: What serum ceruloplasmin screening thresholds rule out versus confirm Wilson's disease?
opts: > 20 mg/dL rules out Wilson's; < 10 mg/dL is confirmatory
> 50 mg/dL rules out Wilson's; < 30 mg/dL is confirmatory
> 10 mg/dL rules out Wilson's; < 2 mg/dL is confirmatory
> 35 mg/dL rules out Wilson's; < 15 mg/dL is confirmatory
items.exp: Screening ceruloplasmin: > 20 mg/dL 'rule out wilsons', 10–20 mg/dL is intermediate, and < 10 mg/dL is 'Confirmatory'. (Book p1016)

items.q: In a patient with an intermediate ceruloplasmin level (10–20 mg/dL), what is the status of total serum copper versus non-ceruloplasmin-bound (free) copper?
opts: Total serum copper is decreased, but non-ceruloplasmin-bound free copper is elevated
Total serum copper and free copper are both markedly increased
Total serum copper is elevated, while free copper is undetectable
Total serum copper and ceruloplasmin-bound copper are both elevated
items.exp: Total serum Cu is decreased because ceruloplasmin-bound Cu (90% normal) is markedly decreased (↓↓), whereas free copper is increased (↑), driving high urinary free copper. (Book p1016)

items.q: What is the critical diagnostic hepatic copper concentration on liver biopsy in Wilson's disease?
items.exp: Quantitative copper estimation on liver biopsy has a 'Critical value : >250 µg/g dry wt.' (Book p1016)

items.q: Which two analytical techniques are specified for quantitative hepatic copper measurement?
opts: Neutron activation analysis or atomic absorption spectrometry
High-performance liquid chromatography or mass spectrometry
Western blotting or enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
items.exp: Quantitative hepatic copper is 'estimated by : Neutron activation Analysis or Atomic absorption spectrometry'. (Book p1016)

items.q: Assess the two statements on serum ceruloplasmin: I Serum ceruloplasmin can be falsely elevated into the normal range during acute inflammation and high-estrogen states like pregnancy. II Non-ceruloplasmin bound copper (NCBC) is used to monitor compliance and efficacy following copper chelation therapy.
items.exp: Both statements are true as noted in the box: acute inflammation/pregnancy cause false elevations, and NCBC monitors therapy. (Book p1016)

items.q: Match each biochemical parameter in Wilson's disease with its diagnostic directional shift — 1) Serum ceruloplasmin and total serum copper 2) Basal 24-hour urine copper and liver biopsy copper … A) Increased (↑) B) Decreased (↓)
items.exp: Biochemical parameters: Serum Ceruloplasmin ↓, Serum Copper ↓, Basal 24 hr urine Cu ↑, and Liver copper ↑. (Book p1016)

items.q: Which triad of laboratory variables forms the Nazar prognostic index for Wilson's acute liver failure?
opts: Serum bilirubin, AST, and Prothrombin time (PT)
Serum copper, ceruloplasmin, and urinary copper
ALT, alkaline phosphatase, and platelet count
items.exp: The Nazar prognostic index comprises S. bilirubin, AST, and PT. (Book p1016)

items.q: What is the drug of choice (DOC) for Wilson's disease, and what is its standard starting and maintenance dose range?
opts: D-Penicillamine; start at 250 mg/day and increase to 1.5 g/day
Trientine; start at 100 mg/day and increase to 500 mg/day
Zinc acetate; start at 10 mg TDS and increase to 50 mg TDS
Tetrathiomolybdate; start at 50 mg daily for life
items.exp: D-Penicillamine is DOC; starting dose is 250 mg/day, increased to 1.5 g/day. (Book p1016)

items.q: Why must oral D-Penicillamine always be taken on an empty stomach?
opts: Food and dietary cations significantly chelate the drug and impair intestinal absorption
It requires gastric hydrochloric acid to convert into its active disulfide form
Food co-ingestion triggers severe immediate anaphylactoid reactions
It directly degrades dietary essential amino acids in the stomach
items.exp: The instructions explicitly specify: 'To be taken empty stomach' because food interferes with bioavailability. (Book p1016)

items.q: Which of the following adverse effects is NOT listed under D-penicillamine therapy?
items.exp: Adverse risks listed are Drug induced lupus erythematosus, membranous nephropathy, myasthenia crisis, Aplastic anemia, and Pyridoxine deficiency (give 25 mg); pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is not listed. (Book p1016)

items.q: What dose of pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) should be co-prescribed with D-penicillamine to prevent deficiency?
items.exp: The book notes: 'Pyridoxine deficiency (Pyridoxine 25 mg to be given)'. (Book p1016)

items.q: Match each anti-copper agent with its specific clinical niche — 1) Trientine 2) Tetrathiomolybdate 3) Zinc … A) 50 mg TDS; induces metallothionein, competes with Cu for DMT-1, preferred in pregnancy B) Chelator for Neurological Wilson's disease (not widely available) C) 1–1.2 g/day; lesser side effects, not available in India, preferred in pregnancy
items.exp: Trientine (1–1.2 g/day) has fewer side effects and is preferred in pregnancy; Tetrathiomolybdate is for Neuro-Wilson's; Zinc (50 mg TDS) induces metallothionein and competes for DMT-1. (Book p1016)
